objective: Review the just-bash backend commit on release/0.3.1/feat/just-bash against the merge-ready bar and its requirements.
scope: Worktree /home/user/holyagent-0.3.1-bash; range git diff ce16cb6..HEAD (one commit). Writer's account: /home/user/holyagent/.git/holyagent/reports/assignment-0mw9n3pas-ln21.md. Spike it follows: /home/user/holyagent/.git/holyagent/reports/assignment-0mw96w93p-53j2.md.

Maintainer (verbatim, 2026-11-09): "didn't we agree on using just-bash as the bash tool backend", "we should also support the just-bash's ts/js capabilities (ts as first option, js as fallback)". No earlier record of that choice was found in the original request, the repository, its issues or the Intents.

Decided (maintainer, 2026-11-09, after research showed just-bash 3.6.0 is a simulated shell that cannot run host executables): "use just-bash and allow the executables on PATH and other relevant places (cross-platform)". The Pi bash tool runs on just-bash (through Pi 1.5.0 BashOperations); commands it does not implement resolve to real executables on PATH and other relevant locations, on Linux, macOS and Windows, so git, bun, bunx, mise, gh, node and the holyagent CLI keep working; just-bash TypeScript execution is offered first and JavaScript is the fallback.

Decided (maintainer, verbatim, 2026-11-09): "about the shadowed commands, prefer them instead of the ones in PATH". Where just-bash implements a command itself (rg, grep, sed, find, tar, diff, awk, jq, ls, xargs and the rest), its built-in runs, and the host executable of the same name is not registered; only commands just-bash lacks pass through to the host.

Maintainer (verbatim, 2026-11-09): "start the spike", "also, billion context's bash safeguards should be turned off if possible". The just-bash spike starts now. Billion Context tool guardrails on the bash tool (default timeout, output cap, repeat detection) are turned off by HolyAgent where Billion Context offers a setting for it; where it does not, the plan says so.

Maintainer (verbatim, 2026-11-09): "everything should be modular and easily upgradeable btw". Each 0.3.1 piece (just-bash backend, host passthrough, TS/JS execution, Codex provider, auto-review, context_management, fff, opencode browse, the screen capability and the capability system) is its own module behind a narrow interface, can be turned off on its own, and every third-party package or binary it uses sits at an exact pin moved only through mise run deps:update, so upgrading one never requires editing the others.

Default (root judgement from spike assignment-0mw96w93p-53j2, revisitable): the just-bash backend runs each shell in a Bun Worker so cancel and Pi's timeout terminate it even in a pure shell loop; it mounts an in-memory /usr/bin and /bin of stubs for host passthrough with the shell PATH set to those and the real PATH given to child processes only; it sets defenseInDepth excludeViolationTypes finalization_registry so ReadWriteFs writes work under Bun; it raises the command, loop, work-unit and js timeout limits; it saves cwd and env even when the command runs exit; it offers host-<name> aliases for host programs a built-in shadows; Windows maps a mount per drive. Billion Context guardrails are turned off by setting BILI_GUARDRAIL_BASH_TIMEOUT=0, BILI_GUARDRAIL_MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES=0 and BILI_GUARDRAIL_REPETITION=0 for the Pi process.

Judge in particular: the departures from the spike (a Bun process per call instead of a Bun Worker, because Pi runs on Node: cost per command and whether state persists correctly; exit losing cwd and env); built-in precedence and passthrough resolution, PATHEXT and .cmd shims on Windows; cancellation and timeout killing the process tree on all three OSes; the guardrail settings written to Billion Context's file only while it is on; the 4.3 MB generated dist/scripts/just-bash.js (is committing it consistent with how the repo ships generated scripts, and is the bundle free of machine paths?); the EXACT_PACKAGES pin path in scripts; and the tests needing bun as the runner executable. Run the built-in /code-review on ce16cb6...HEAD (explicit range) and mise run verify in the worktree.
constraints: Do not check out other commits in any checkout and make no edits.
Report in under 450 words; mark each finding blocking or non-blocking with file and line.

criteria.text: The just-bash backend meets its requirements on Linux, macOS and Windows as far as code and tests show
Turning the capability off restores Pi's own bash and nothing else changes
Tests cover the change and fail without it

result:
result: Two blockers, 5 non-blocking findings. `mise run verify` exits 0 (2904 pass, 0 fail, check, lint and fmt clean). I could not run Windows or macOS.

**Built-in `/code-review`:** it ran, but it reviewed the wrong tree. All 7 findings cite `setup/capabilities.ts`, `setup/pi-install.ts`, `setup/tui/session.ts` and form-aware `toolArgs`. None of those are in `ce16cb6..HEAD`. The `config/capabilities.ts` finding is about scaffolding that predates this commit. Rejected all 7 as out of range.

**Blocking**
1. **Programs given by path do not run** (behavior).
   - `shell.ts:357`: the shell `PATH` is fixed at `/usr/bin:/bin`, and only stubs are registered. I ran `./elf hello` in the built bundle. just-bash parses the binary as a script and fails with `unexpected EOF`, exit 2.
   - The same applies to `./node_modules/.bin/tsc` (a shebang JS file), `./target/debug/app` and `./a.out`.
   - `export PATH=/x:$PATH; tool` never finds a native `tool` either, because host lookup uses the request-time `PATH`.
   - `docs/pi/shell.md:18` and `guidelines.ts` admit this ("run it by name or through bunx").
   - It is a real regression against Pi's bash and against "executables on PATH and other relevant places". The root can accept it as a documented limitation or ask for a fix.
2. **Turning the capability off leaves Billion Context's guardrails disabled** (regressions).
   - `capabilities.ts:355` writes `guardrails.{bashTimeout:0, maxOutputBytes:0, repetition:false}` to the Billion Context file, with no revert path.
   - After `--just-bash off`, Pi's own bash still has no default timeout, output cap or repeat breaker.
   - `docs/pi/shell.md:39` states this. It breaks "restores Pi's own bash and nothing else changes". The environment variables do revert (`tools.ts:155`).

**Non-blocking**
**`exit` drops cwd and env** (`shell.ts:411`). I confirmed it: `cd /usr; export B=2; unset A; exit 3` returns exit 3 with empty changes and cwd unchanged. The root's default said to keep state on `exit`; the writer disclosed the miss and `guidelines.ts` documents it.
**Output order** (`shell.ts:394-397`). Non-streaming runs send all stdout, then all stderr, so interleaving differs from real bash.
**Concurrent calls** (`bash.ts:178`). Shared `state` is last-write-wins if Pi runs two bash calls at once.
**`rg --version` fails** (disclosed). Each call also scans every `PATH` folder, which costs about 0.2 s per call here, in line with the docs' ~100 ms startup claim.
**Untested on Windows:** registering the tool after session start, `.cmd` shim spawning, drive mounts and `taskkill` are unit-tested on their pure parts only, or not at all.

**Checked and fine**
**Process per call:** state persists correctly for `cd` and `export`. The abort, timeout and grandchild-kill tests pass. The kill is `process.kill(-pid)` on POSIX and `taskkill /T` on Windows.
**Precedence:** built-ins win, `host-<name>` aliases cover shadowed programs, and relative `PATH` entries are ignored.
**TypeScript first:** `js-exec` TypeScript worked in my runs, including code on stdin.
**Bundle:** committing `dist/scripts/just-bash.js` matches how `holyagent.js` ships (1 MB). Its only `/home/user` and `/root` hits are just-bash's virtual defaults, so there are no machine paths. `sql.js` is stubbed.
**Pin:** `EXACT_PACKAGES` pins `just-bash` at exact `3.6.0`, with a test.
**Tests:** they need `bun` as the runner executable, which is acceptable under mise.

evidence:
The just-bash backend meets its requirements on Linux, macOS and Windows as far as code and tests show: blocker 1 above (`shell.ts:357`, reproduced on the bundle). The rest holds on Linux only. `bash.test.ts` and `bash-shell.test.ts` pass, and Windows is covered only by pure-function tests.
Turning the capability off restores Pi's own bash and nothing else changes: blocker 2 above (`capabilities.ts:355`). Pi's own operations are restored (`bash.ts:114`, tested at `bash.test.ts:229`).
Tests cover the change and fail without it: the 3 new test files cover passthrough, precedence, abort, timeout, process-tree kill, TypeScript/JavaScript and the guardrails. No test covers `exit` state or path-given binaries. `mise run verify` exit 0, log at `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-holyagent/43946df6-456d-58c6-bea3-7e958fcb9495/scratchpad/verify.log`.
findings: see the Blocking and Non-blocking lists above.
